title: Impact of Welfare Eligibility on Labor Supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Why this method?  
• Welfare eligibility is assigned mechanically at an income threshold (the cutoff in the running variable “running_var”).  
• Individuals just below and just above the threshold are assumed to be comparable, so any discontinuous jump in average hours worked (y) at the cutoff can be interpreted as the causal effect of eligibility.

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: In the absence of the policy, the conditional expectation of potential outcomes varies smoothly with income at the threshold.  
2. No precise manipulation: Individuals cannot perfectly sort their reported income around the cutoff.  
3. Correct functional form / bandwidth choice is addressed with data-driven bandwidth selection and alternative specifications as robustness checks.

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################
# Impact of Welfare Eligibility on Labor Supply
# Sharp RDD at the income cutoff
###############################################

# 0) Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
needed <- c("rdrobust", "rddensity", "ggplot2")
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for(p in needed){
  if(!(p %in% installed)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

# 1) Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s92_data.csv")

# 2) Define cutoff ----------------------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0.5                       # based on codebook & preview
df$running_centered <- df$running_var - cutoff

# 3) Main sharp RDD (local linear, MSE-optimal bandwidth) -------------------
main_rdd <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_centered, c = 0)

cat("\n=== Main RDD Estimate (Local Linear, MSE-optimal h) ===\n")
print(main_rdd$coef[1])             # treatment effect at cutoff
cat("Robust 95% CI: [",
    main_rdd$ci[1,1], ",", main_rdd$ci[1,2], "]\n\n")

# 4) Robustness checks ------------------------------------------------------

## 4a) Quadratic specification
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_centered, p = 2, c = 0)
cat("Quadratic local polynomial estimate:", rdd_quad$coef[1], "\n")

## 4b) Manual smaller bandwidth (h = 0.1)
rdd_smallh <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_centered, h = 0.1, c = 0)
cat("Estimate with h = 0.1:", rdd_smallh$coef[1], "\n")

## 4c) Placebo cutoff at 0.3
placebo_cut <- 0.3
rdd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y,
                        x = df$running_var - placebo_cut,
                        c = 0)
cat("Placebo cutoff estimate (should be ~0):", rdd_placebo$coef[1], "\n")

## 4d) Density test (McCrary)
dens <- rddensity(X = df$running_centered, c = 0)
cat("\n=== McCrary Density Test ===\n")
print(dens$test)

# 5) Simple visualization ---------------------------------------------------
ggplot(df, aes(x = running_centered, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(df, running_centered < 0),
              method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(df, running_centered >= 0),
              method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Hours Worked around Welfare Eligibility Cutoff",
       x = "Income minus cutoff", y = "Hours worked (standardized)")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic theory predicts that receiving welfare benefits lowers the marginal benefit of work, so eligibility should reduce labor supply. I therefore expect:  
• Sign: Negative discontinuity (treated – control < 0).  
• Magnitude: Roughly −0.20 to −0.30 standard-deviation units of hours worked, large enough to be statistically significant with 500 observations close to the cutoff.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Examine changes in labor supply around the income threshold for welfare eligibility.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the income threshold for welfare eligibility results in a reduction in labor supply.
